t:
The Secretary of the Army is hereby authorized and directed to cause surveys to be made at the following named localities and subject to all applicable provisions of section 110 of the River and Harbor Act of 1950:
Mexico Beach, Florida.
Great Lakes, particularly Lake Ontario and Lake Erie, in connection with water supply, pollution abatement, navigation, flood control, hydroelectric power, and related water resources development and control.

fable.w: The section only directs the Secretary of the Army to have surveys made at named localities, subject to an existing statutory provision. The tempting reading is that surveys on water supply, pollution abatement and flood control would involve states or local interests, but the text requires no consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body, rulemaking, or right to sue involving anyone outside the federal government. It is a federal study directive, not participation in a federal decision.
fable.s: The Secretary of the Army is hereby authorized and directed to cause surveys to be made at the following named localities

qwen_block.w: This section authorizes the Secretary of the Army to conduct surveys. It does not require consultation with, or participation by, any non-federal entities such as states, tribes, the public, or private organizations. The action is purely internal to the federal government.
qwen_block.s: The Secretary of the Army is hereby authorized and directed to cause surveys to be made at the following named localities and subject to all applicable provisions of section 110 of the River and Harbor Act of 1950:

opus.w: The section only directs the Secretary of the Army, a federal official, to conduct surveys at named places; no state, local government, expert or member of the public is consulted, heard, or given a role in any federal decision. The general cross-reference to section 110 of the River and Harbor Act of 1950 does not itself set up any hearing, consultation or comment process in this text, so it cannot by itself support a participation finding.
opus.s: The Secretary of the Army is hereby authorized and directed to cause surveys to be made at the following named localities and subject to all applicable provisions of section 110 of the River and Harbor Act of 1950
opus.b:
I'm labelling this **No**, with moderate confidence.

**Step 1 – the tempting reading.** The cross-reference to "all applicable provisions of section 110 of the River and Harbor Act of 1950" could be read as bringing in outside participation. Older river and harbor laws sometimes required consulting states or holding local hearings for Corps surveys. But the section itself names no outside party and no hearing, comment period or advisory body. I can't confirm from the text alone what section 110 requires, so I'm not treating the reference as a participation requirement. On its face, the section only tells the Secretary of the Army to conduct surveys, which is federal action with no outside party involved.

qwen_chat.w: The section authorizes the Secretary of the Army to conduct surveys at specific locations. It does not require consultation, coordination, or input from any parties outside the federal government (such as states, tribes, or the public) before making a decision. Conducting a survey is an internal fact-finding activity, not a participatory process involving external stakeholders.
qwen_chat.s: The Secretary of the Army is hereby authorized and directed to cause surveys to be made at the following named localities
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that "surveys" imply gathering data from the public or local entities, thus constituting participation. However, the text only authorizes the Secretary to cause surveys to be made; it does not mandate consultation, public comment, or coordination with outside parties. The surveys are likely technical/engineering assessments conducted by federal employees or contractors, which falls under internal government action.
